title: Why you should never connect directly to a Pod IP
caption: ClusterIP services explained in plain English. How do you route internal traffic in your cluster?

scenes.vo: Never connect directly to Pod IPs. Pods die constantly, and every new replacement gets a completely different address.
scenes.heading: CLUSTERIP

scenes.vo: Think of a ClusterIP like an office switchboard. Callers dial one central number, and it forwards you to an available desk.
scenes.heading: THE ANALOGY
scenes.line: ONE NUMBER ROUTING TO ANY DESK

scenes.vo: Your frontend sends requests to the ClusterIP service. The service automatically balances that traffic across all matching backend Pods.
scenes.heading: TRAFFIC FLOW

scenes.vo: If a backend Pod crashes, Kubernetes updates the endpoints instantly. Your callers never notice a single dropped packet.
scenes.heading: POD CRASHES?

scenes.vo: To create one quickly, expose your Deployment. Kubernetes assigns an internal ClusterIP by default.
scenes.heading: QUICK COMMAND

scenes.vo: So remember: stable virtual IP, internal traffic routing, and zero downtime. Follow for more Kubernetes made simple.
scenes.heading: CLUSTERIP
